name: SUBSoNIC
question: Does subsensory sacral neuromodulation reduce weekly fecal incontinence episodes compared with sham stimulation after permanent implantation?

arms.label: sham stimulation through the implanted device

design.population: Adults aged 18–80 years with refractory fecal incontinence who responded to test stimulation and received a permanent sacral neuromodulator.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind randomized crossover superiority trial
design.locator: Full text, Methods: Trial design, Eligibility criteria, and Allocation and blinding

verdictNote: The primary comparison missed significance with complete diaries from only 16 participants.
takeaway: In 39 implanted adults with refractory fecal incontinence, subsensory sacral neuromodulation versus sham stimulation did not significantly reduce weekly incontinence episodes in the 16 with complete crossover diaries (mean difference −0.795 episodes; 95% CI −1.5 to 0.0; P = 0.06).

reports.label: Crossover trial and 58-week cohort follow-up
reports.citation: Vollebregt PF, Goh YL, Bagul A, et al. "Clinical efficacy of subsensory sacral neuromodulation in adults with faecal incontinence: The SUBSoNIC crossover randomised controlled trial and cohort follow-up study." *Colorectal Dis.* 2025;27(11):e70308. doi:10.1111/codi.70308
reports.followUp: Two 16-week blinded crossover periods; open-label cohort follow-up to 58 weeks

results.measure: Mean episodes per week in final four weeks of each crossover period; mean difference, subsensory SNM minus sham
results.note: The abstract gives −0.795; Table 2 rounds the mean difference to −0.7. Paired analysis included 16 participants with complete data in both periods.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Results; full text, Table 2 and Results: Primary outcome

results.measure: Sensitivity-analysis mean difference, subsensory SNM minus sham, imputing blank diary items as zero when another item was completed that day
results.note: Missing-day imputation changed the inference; this was a sensitivity analysis, not the primary analysis.
results.locator: Full text, Results: Primary outcome; Figure 2; supplementary Table S9 cited in text

results.measure: Mean episodes per week during crossover; mean difference, subsensory SNM minus sham
results.note: Urgency without incontinence; no significant between-treatment difference.

results.measure: Mean episodes per week in open-label cohort at baseline and 58 weeks
results.note: Within-cohort comparison; patients chose subsensory or suprasensory stimulation during open-label follow-up.
results.locator: Full text, Table 3 and Results: Cohort follow-up

harms.label: Adverse events during crossover and cohort follow-up
harms.locator: Full text, Results: Adverse events (crossover and cohort follow-up)
harms.note: The article reports event count, not the number of affected patients; types are in supplementary Table S12, unavailable in the extracted local text.

harms.label: Serious adverse device events
harms.locator: Full text, Results: Adverse events (crossover and cohort follow-up)
harms.note: The reported serious adverse device event did not require overnight hospitalization; treatment period was not specified.

delivery.label: Randomized sequences and outcome completion
delivery.value: 17 randomized to active then sham and 22 to sham then active; 9 and 7, respectively, completed both primary-outcome diaries; 19/39 completed 58-week follow-up.

delivery.label: Implantation and lead-placement criteria
delivery.value: Test stimulation preceded randomization; responders received an InterStim II pulse generator with fluoroscopy-guided S3 or S4 lead placement and low-voltage motor responses at at least three of four electrodes.

delivery.label: Programming and sham
delivery.value: Active stimulation used 14 Hz and 210 μs, with amplitude below the habituated sensory threshold; sham amplitude was 0 or 0.05 V. Reprogramming was scheduled six weeks after each period began.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods: Active stimulation and SHAM stimulation

delivery.label: Study discontinuation
delivery.value: Enrollment stopped July 24, 2022, after 39/90 planned randomizations because COVID-19 disruptions impeded recruitment, visits, and surgery.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods: Sample size; Results: Participants
